       testing, commissioning, and readiness of such facilities. Any delay or failure by
       Transmission Customer to perform its obligations may result in a corresponding delay in
       the requested in-service date, for which Transmission Provider shall not be held liable.

11.0   ADJUSTMENT FOR LOSSES
       To the extent any Delivery Point is at a voltage level less than 44 kV or the metering
       point(s) is (are) remote from the Delivery Point, the load associated with such Delivery
       Point used for the calculation of the Network Integration Transmission Service charge
       shall be adjusted for the losses associated with: (i) the Transmission Provider's
       applicable distribution and/or transmission facilities; and/or (ii) the Transmission
       Customer's distribution and transmission facilities, as applicable. Such loss
       compensation factors shall be as mutually agreed upon by the Parties. To the extent the
       Parties cannot agree on any such factors, the Dispute Resolution Procedures in Section
       12 of the Tariff may be invoked to resolve the disagreement.

12.0   BREACH, CURE AND DEFAULT
       A breach of this Service Agreement shall include (a) the failure to provide and maintain
       security when due and (b) the failure to pay any amount when due. Upon a breach, the non-
       breaching Party shall give written notice of such breach to the breaching Party. The
       breaching Party shall have thirty (30) calendar days from receipt of the notice to cure the
       breach.

       If a breach is not cured within the 30-day period, (1) the breaching Party is automatically in
       default of this Service Agreement and (2) the non-breaching Party shall be relieved of any
       further applicable obligation, subject to the requirements of 18 CFR § 35.15 as applicable,
       and is entitled to recover from the breaching Party all amounts due hereunder, plus all other
       damages and remedies to which it is entitled at law or in equity. Transmission Provider may
       draw on security if an event of default has occurred or is ongoing and any applicable cure
       period has passed, or security in the form of a letter of credit is within 30 days of expiration
       and Transmission Customer has not provided Transmission Provider with an amendment
       extending the expiration of the letter of credit. Transmission Provider reserves the right to not
       reduce security if an event of default has occurred or is ongoing, or if Transmission Customer
       has not made all required payments.

13.0   NO WAIVERS
       Failure of a Party to enforce any provision of this Service Agreement will not be
       construed as a waiver of such provision, and will not affect the validity of the Service
       Agreement or the right of either Party subsequently to enforce any provision of the
       Service Agreement. Any waiver at any time by either Party of its rights with respect to
       the other Party or with respect to any matter arising in connection with this Service
       Agreement will not be considered a waiver with respect to any subsequent matter.
       Failure of a Party to resort to any legal remedy or to exercise any one or more alternative
       remedies will not affect such Party's right subsequently to resort to any one or more of
       such rights or remedies on account of any such grounds then existing or which may
       subsequently occur.
 14.0   ACCEPTANCE BY FERC
       The Parties recognize that this Service Agreement must be filed with the Commission
       and is subject to the jurisdiction of that Commission. Transmission Provider shall have
       the right to make a unilateral filing with the Commission to modify this Service
       Agreement with respect to any rates, terms and conditions, charges, classifications of
       service, rule or regulation under section 205 or any other applicable provision of the
       Federal Power Act and the Commission’s rules and regulations thereunder, and
       Transmission Customer shall have the right to make a unilateral filing with the

      Transmission Provider will bill Transmission Customer monthly with actual project

 5.2 Actual Revenue Contribution. Transmission Customer’s “Actual Revenue
Contribution” for each billing year during the 15-year period described in Section 5.1 is the
amount the Transmission Customer actually paid for the New Network Load at the [POD
Name] [Delivery Voltage]kV Delivery Point on a monthly basis in the applicable year based on
actual monthly load and billing determinants applied to the applicable transmission rate after

5.3 Transmission Customer Shortfall Event and Payment Obligation. Beginning on June
1 of the first calendar year following the in-service date of all Network Upgrades to
accommodate the new Network Load and continuing each billing year thereafter until the
expiration of the 15-year term described in Section 5.1, Transmission Provider shall determine
whether the Transmission Customer’s Actual Revenue Contribution equals or exceeds the
Committed Revenue Contribution for the prior billing year subject to the calculation of the
Committed Revenue Contribution described in Section 5.1 for any applicable months prior to
June 1 in which Network Upgrades were placed in-service. In the event that the Transmission
Customer’s Actual Revenue Contribution in a billing year is less than its Committed Revenue
Contribution for that same billing year, a “Transmission Customer Shortfall Event” has
occurred for that billing year. If a Transmission Customer Shortfall Event occurs, the
Transmission Customer shall pay an amount equal to the difference between the Actual
Revenue Contribution and the Committed Revenue Contribution (“Transmission Customer
Shortfall Payment Obligation”).

5.4 Illustrative Example. For example, if the new Network Load is 200 MW and the
applicable transmission rate is $2,500/MW-month, the Transmission Customer’s Committed
Revenue Contribution for that new Network Load at the identified Delivery Point would be
$4,500,000 (((200 MW * .75) * $2,500/MW-month) * 12 months). If in each month of a
billing year, the monthly load and billing determinants used for determining actual network
integration transmission service charges for service at that Delivery Point was 100 MW, then
the Actual Revenue Contribution would be $3,000,000 ((100 MW * $2,500/MW-month) * 12
months); therefore, a Transmission Customer Shortfall Event for that billing year would have
occurred and the Transmission Customer Shortfall Payment Obligation would be $1,500,000
($4,500,000 - $3,000,000). However, if in each month of a billing year, the monthly load and
billing determinates used for determining actual network integration transmission service
charges was 180 MW, then the Actual Revenue Contribution would be $5,400,000 (180 MW *
$2,500/MW-month) * 12 months), no Transmission Customer Shortfall Event would have
occurred for that year and there would be no Transmission Customer Shortfall Payment
Obligation for that billing year.

5.5 Timing of Payment. Transmission Customer shall make payment of the Transmission
Customer Shortfall Payment Obligation to the Transmission Provider within 20 days of receipt
of an invoice to be issued by the Transmission Provider following its annual calculation of the
Transmission Customer Shortfall Payment Obligation. Transmission Provider will conduct
such calculation as soon as reasonably practicable following the end of each billing year after
the in-service date of the Network Upgrade needed to accommodate the new Network Load.

5.6 Transmission Customer Shortfall Payment Obligation Calculated Each Applicable
Billing Year During Term. The Transmission Customer Shortfall Payment Obligation shall
apply solely to the aggregate liability of Transmission Customer for a Transmission Customer
Shortfall Event arising during that specific billing year. Payment by Transmission Customer

 of the Transmission Customer Shortfall Payment Obligation in any billing year shall not be
construed to limit, waive, or otherwise affect the Transmission Provider’s right to recover the
Transmission Customer Shortfall Payment Obligation for Transmission Customer Shortfall
Events occurring in any subsequent billing year during the Term of this Service Agreement.
Each billing year during the Term of this Service Agreement shall be treated independently for
purposes of calculating and enforcing the Transmission Customer Shortfall Payment
Obligation. For clarity, any Transmission Customer Shortfall Events occurring in different
billing years during the Term of this Service Agreement shall each give rise to separate
payment obligations up to the Transmission Customer Shortfall Payment Obligation applicable
for the respective year in which the shortfall event occurred.
